newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar punishes free-falling mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar punishes free-falling mark.

text.p: The dollar continued its impressive rally to a six-year high against the mark as the German unit suffered heavy losses across the board.
Technical analysts said the dollar and sterling rallies versus the mark show no signs of slowing.

"We've seen a lot of mark weakness across the board. Yesterday we saw a big correction in the mark crosses, now we're seeing the trend (higher) reestablished," said Kalpana Patel, global head of technical analysis at Swiss Bank.
The dollar's 71-month high at 1.7742 marks coincided with an 81-month high at 3.0010 in sterling/mark.

Chartists struggled to identify current upside targets for dollar/mark, though 1.78 represents a 61.8-percent Fibonacci retracement of the drop from a June 1989 high at 2.05 to the post-World War II low at 1.3438 in March 1995.

"A lot of people are asking what's above here, but I don't really know. There really isn't much up here until you get to around 1.80 and my long-term objective is 1.82," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
Sterling enjoys very good support at 2.9975 marks, with pending resistance at 301.50 and a big-figure target at 3.05, chartists said.
"The 3.00 level has been talked about and there are some people taking profits there. So sterling/mark has stalled temporarily, but it's still in an uptrend," said Patel.
Mark/lira has also slunk lower, testing 970, with the current resistance seen near 969.50. The mark has suffered against virtually every cross in recent trade.
"Sterling/mark is screaming and the other mark/crosses are getting crushed," Johnson said.
Yet the failure of dollar/Swiss to follow dollar/mark higher clearly shows that the mark's weakness, not dollar strength, is propelling the dollar higher, Johnson added.
"That's the only thing that bothers me. Dollar/Swiss is still 300 points off its high," at 1.4922 in March, he added.
Mark/yen remains heavily oversold and may briefly blip higher in coming sessions, chartists said.
"I wouldn't want to be bearish mark/yen down here," said Johnson.
But the dollar/mark advance leaves mark/yen susceptible to fresh carnage, Patel argued.
"Having had a correction (early Friday), we can continue with the downside as long as dollar/mark continues to go higher," she added. ((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
